_comment: Pinned INPUT manifest for scripts/build_fingerprint_corpus.py. It says which upstream
releases to download and which of their files to hash. The built index is a separate
artifact and is deliberately NOT committed: bomwerk ships the matcher and this manifest,
Every `commit` is the DEREFERENCED commit of `ref`, that is refs/tags/<ref>^{} for an
annotated tag. Pinning an annotated tag's own object id by mistake still fetches the right
tree, which hides the error, so the builder re-resolves each ref against the remote and
fails when the two disagree. Never hand-write a commit id: run
Releases are chosen, not enumerated. The index exists to identify OLD vendored copies, so
each library pins the versions people actually vendor plus any version a widely cited CVE
sits in. Pinning every tag would turn a few megabytes of index into hundreds.
`tier` selects a profile: 0 = smoke (what the nightmare corpus and the tests need),
1 = demo, 2 = all. See K_PROFILE_MAX_TIER in the builder.
A library is listed here only when upstream publishes a real version for it. stb is
deliberately absent: upstream has no tags, so the only version a corpus could assert is a
commit id, and bomwerk already names it `stb` from its folder. Asserting a commit as the
version would contradict the nightmare answer key and buy nothing.

libraries.name: zlib
libraries.why: the most-vendored C library; nightmare pins v1.2.11, whose deflate.c and inflate.c carry CVE-2018-25032 and CVE-2022-37434

libraries.name: freertos
libraries.why: the fork case: nightmare vendors V11.1.0 with one modified list.c while its version header still reads V11.1.0, and no tool in the comparison notices

libraries.name: uthash
libraries.why: header-only, so a single file decides its identity; nightmare's copy is reported with no version today because the heuristic has no row for it

libraries.name: cjson
libraries.why: writes its version only as three numeric macros, so no quoted-string heuristic can ever read it; nightmare reports it as the folder name cjson-prebuilt with no version

libraries.name: mbedtls
libraries.why: the TLS stack vendored into firmware, and one of the eight libraries T93 names; vendor SDKs ship modified copies of it. License left empty on purpose: upstream is dual-licensed (Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later) and one SPDX id here would flatten it, the gap docs/nightmare-corpus.md already records for stb

libraries.name: lwip
libraries.why: the TCP/IP stack vendored into firmware, also named by T93; ESP-IDF and vendor SDKs carry forks of it
